items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions Cozy Cole as an example of a black musician brought into the studios; INTERVIEWEE does not mention Cozy Cole or indicate a personal connection.

ctx.x: Because I used to get criticism from even guys in the studio saying, you know, you've been taking lessons, that's really sort of taking unfair advantage. Honest to God, another trumpet player in New York said that to me. So in the beginning, they sort of did that.

I can go back even before that, there weren't Jimmy, when/any black musicians in the studios -- and then all of a sudden we've got some powers that be, some friends of the black society, tried to get some black musicians in. And of course they did, eventually, the Ben Websters and the Charlie Shavers and guys of that category, Teddy Wilson, were brought into the studios and when they had shown -- Cozy Cole -- show they could qualify. And these musicians have always been known, black or white, to be the epitome of…

Sure. You know, I think jazz musicians would come in, and you would get your friends in. If your friends were black, you would bring them in. I remember I was doing the Patti Page show and asking for a trumpet section, and one time sitting there and Ernie Royal said, what the hell are you doing here? I said, what do you mean, what am I doing here? I got all you guys here.
